Wash at 40 degrees with a little less detergent than usual, and skip the fabric softener, as it coats the fibres and makes them less absorbent. Tumble drying on low keeps them fluffy, and a good shake before hanging them helps if you dry them on a line.

turns.user: Found the label: it says 'Moss bath towel, lake blue'. So there's nothing wrong with them at all. That's just their colour! I ordered grey. You've sent me the wrong colour. I feel a bit silly now for calling it a stain.

turns.user: Okay. Are the grey ones exactly the same quality? The blue ones feel really thick, and that's partly why I chose them over the cheaper ones.

They're also the same size: 70 by 140 centimetres for the bath towels. If anything, darker colours can feel a touch firmer at first, but that goes after the first wash.

turns.user: The thing is, I've got guests arriving on 12 December, and I wanted the new towels out for them. Will they be here in time? I'd rather not put out the old ones; they're properly worn out.

turns.user: Good to know. Can the collection be on a Saturday? I work long hours during the week, and I'm hardly ever home before eight.

turns.user: Thanks. Do towel colours fade much? My old towels went patchy after a year or so, and I'd like these to last.
turns.assistant: Some fading over the years is normal for cotton, but you can slow it down. Wash the towels with similar colours, at 40 degrees rather than hotter, and keep bleach and whitening detergents away from them. Drying them in strong sunlight fades them faster, so dry them indoors or in the shade when you can. Patchiness usually comes from skincare products, such as those with benzoyl peroxide, which bleach cotton. Rinse face washes off your hands before reaching for a towel, and the colour will hold up much longer.
